screening_results.reason: This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that investigates logical reasoning/contradiction identification—a goal-directed cognitive task requiring participants to determine whether a conclusion contradicts a premise (i.e., a problem-solving judgment). The study reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects fMRI analyses, provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space for task-related BOLD activation, and includes voxelwise results presented in figures/tables with statistical thresholds. Behavioral and BOLD contrasts are reported and BOLD analyses are explicitly described. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not patient-group comparisons only, includes healthy-group task effects, and is empirical). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants using a pattern-discovery (inductive reasoning) task that meets the definition of problem solving (goal: discover a category; need to infer how to reach it). The study reports group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses using SPM with MNI normalization, FWE-corrected voxelwise results, and BOLD fMRI data. The manuscript indicates voxelwise activation results (domain contrasts, conjunctions) that would be reported in tables/figures (methods describe MNI template and BA/atlas localization). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not between-group-only, not a review). Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present.

This paper is a whole-brain task-based fMRI study reporting stereotactic coordinates and BOLD results (meets I7, I8) and provides voxelwise results in text/figures (meets I9). However, it does not meet the review’s focus on problem-solving in healthy adults (I5): the tasks are verbal fluency and mental rotation, which are cognitive but not clearly defined here as problem-solving tasks per the review definition. Critically, the study population includes clinical (Asperger Syndrome) and healthy control groups and the reported whole-brain group-level results are primarily contrasts involving the clinical group (diagnosis and diagnosis-by-sex interactions); there are no standalone whole-brain task activation results reported for a healthy adult group alone. Thus it violates exclusion criterion E5 (includes only between-group contrasts / does not provide healthy-group task effects). Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criteria not met: I5, I6. Exclusion criterion met: E5.

Although this is an empirical, whole-brain task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that reports BOLD results and stereotactic (Talairach) coordinates, the task is a visuospatial angle-discrimination judgment (ANGLE vs. COLOR). This is a perceptual/decision discrimination task rather than a problem-solving task as defined (having a goal and needing to figure out a way to reach it). Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (problem-solving task) is not met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants using the Hit-N sequential game (a goal-directed problem-solving task: reach the final position by planning moves). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM analyses (rfxGLM) and presents voxelwise activation maps and cluster results (including FDR thresholds). Stereotactic coordinates are reported in Talairach space (e.g., VLPFC at 47, 40, 3; insula/striatum coordinates described), and the imaging modality is BOLD fMRI with whole-brain preprocessing and analysis described. Voxelwise results are presented in figures and described in text. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study of clinical reasoning (MCQ diagnostic problem solving) in healthy adult physicians and interns, which meets the review’s problem-solving definition (goal-directed diagnostic decisions). The study reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses with second-level/group effects (random-effects, conjunction and direct group comparisons) and family-wise error cluster correction. Anatomical scans were registered to Talairach space and results are reported with Talairach coordinates (figures/tables referenced). The imaging analysis is BOLD-based fMRI (percent-change-from-mean). Task-related activations are reported in the main text and figures/tables, satisfying coordinate reporting and acceptable presentation formats. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, disease-only, non-empirical) are met.

This is an empirical task-based BOLD fMRI study using a matrix reasoning (problem-solving) task in healthy adults (N=34). The paper reports whole-brain, random-effects group analyses (voxelwise GLM with FDR correction), provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI/Talairach (tables/ROI coordinates described), and includes BOLD analyses. The task fits the definition of problem solving (goal-directed matrix problems). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion sections. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5–I9 and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This study is a task-based fMRI investigation of linear-order reasoning (a problem-solving/inference task) in adult participants, including healthy (non-depressed) controls. It reports whole-brain, group-level mixed-effects analyses (within ND group and D–ND comparisons) using voxelwise cluster-corrected thresholds, and provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space for activation peaks. The imaging modality is BOLD fMRI, and voxelwise results are reported (main text and supplementary tables/figures). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not non-empirical, includes healthy-group task effects).

The study is an empirical, task-based fMRI investigation using the Raven's Progressive Matrices, a problem-solving/analogical reasoning task (meets I5). It includes a healthy adult control group and reports whole-brain, group-level activation maps for the control (NC) group and combined analyses (meets I6). Analyses were performed in MNI space and peak coordinates/locations are reported (meets I7). The study uses BOLD fMRI with voxelwise whole-brain results (meets I8). Task-related voxelwise results are reported in main text/figures and are available as stereotactic results (meets I9). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only (E3), not solely disease/age/gender comparisons (E4), include healthy-group task effects rather than only between-group contrasts (E5), and it is empirical original data (not E6). Therefore the article should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults using a picture-puzzle task that meets the definition of problem solving (clear goal: find differences; need to figure out how to reach it). The sample comprises healthy adults (N=64). The analysis includes second-level, whole-brain random-effects ANOVAs (group-level effects). Results report stereotactic coordinates for activation peaks (e.g., anterior striatum, midbrain, rLPFC) and reference supplementary tables; BOLD responses were modeled and analyzed. Voxelwise/whole-brain results are presented and small-volume corrections are reported, satisfying reporting requirements. The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not a non-empirical paper, includes within-healthy-group task effects). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review and is included.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of problem solving (arithmetic word problems requiring a goal and steps to reach it). It reports whole-brain, group-level BOLD analyses in healthy adult participants (n=36 analyzed), with voxelwise results reported in MNI stereotactic space (coordinate tables/figures) using SPM8. The paper includes whole-brain statistical thresholds and cluster-level FWE correction and reports task-related BOLD increases. The full text (background, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, patient-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation in healthy adults using a representation-matching task (goal-directed comparison of symbolic equations and charts, including a condition requiring calculation), which qualifies as a problem-solving task under the review definition. It reports whole-brain, random-effects group analyses (two-sample t-tests) on healthy adult participants, uses BOLD fMRI, and provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (tables/figures). All required voxelwise results are reported. No exclusion criteria were met: results are not ROI-only, participants are healthy adults, and the study is empirical. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so content is complete.

Excluded because this is a single-subject (n=1) case study of a 16-year-old abacus expert; no group-level healthy adult whole-brain fMRI effects are reported. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (doesn't include any healthy-group task effect / only single-subject). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI study of a mental addition task which meets a goal-directed computation), I7 (reports stereotactic normalization to MNI space and lists coordinates), I8 (reports BOLD fMRI analyses), I9 (voxelwise results reported and available). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (requires at least one whole-brain analysis with group-level effects in healthy adult individuals) — not satisfied because only one adolescent subject and no group-level statistics. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is a task-based fMRI study using Raven's Progressive Matrices (a problem-solving/fluid reasoning task), with whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM) and group-level within-group effects reported for the healthy comparison group. BOLD-based analyses and psychophysiological interaction (PPI) connectivity results are reported. The manuscript indicates stereotactic peak coordinates were identified (seed coordinates and peak activations) and presents voxelwise results in figures/tables. Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Note: sample age range (14–36) includes some adolescents, and exact coordinate values are not shown in the provided excerpt, so confidence is moderate.

Excluded because the study does not meet key inclusion criteria for this meta-analysis. While it is a task-based fMRI study reporting BOLD results and stereotactic coordinates in healthy adult controls (I7, I8) and reporting voxelwise results in the main text (I9), it does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined (mental rotation is a visuospatial transformation task rather than a goal-directed problem-solving paradigm) (I5 not met). Additionally, all reported fMRI analyses were hypothesis-driven ROI (small-volume) analyses rather than unbiased whole-brain group-level analyses (I6 not met), triggering exclusion criterion E3 (reports only ROI results). Full text appears complete. Therefore the paper must be excluded.

This is a task-based BOLD fMRI study in healthy adult participants that uses a math calculation task (goal-directed computation) fitting the problem-solving definition. The paper reports whole-brain, random-effects group analyses and voxelwise results with MNI stereotactic coordinates, and BOLD (fMRI) activation contrasts are presented (tables/figures and ROI follow-ups). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so appears complete. Therefore it satisfies I5–I9.

This study does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined by the review (a goal followed by a need to figure out a way to reach it). It examines social truth-telling and evaluative judgments (social vs simple truth questions) rather than problem-solving across domains. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI analysis), I7 (reports stereotactic MNI coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis reported), I9 (voxelwise results reported in text/figures/tables). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (task-based problem solving). No exclusion criteria were triggered (not ROI-only, includes healthy-group task effects, not a non-empirical paper). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of visuo-spatial reasoning (a problem-solving task with goal and steps), conducted in healthy adult participants (n=20). The study reports whole-brain voxelwise group-level analyses (GLM, group-level contrast maps) with normalization to MNI space and identifies ROIs based on group contrasts; BOLD fMRI was used. Coordinates/activation maps are reported/indicated. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, includes healthy-group task effects). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This fMRI study examines clinical reasoning (MCQ diagnosis task) which is a problem-solving task (goal: determine diagnosis; requires devising a way to reach it). It uses task-based whole-brain BOLD fMRI with group-level voxelwise analyses (second-level AFNI 3dttest++), reports stereotactic Talairach coordinates and t/p values for task-related activation and covariates, and presents BOLD (percent-change) results corrected for multiple comparisons. Participants are healthy adult physicians (residents and faculty). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not non-empirical, includes within-group healthy task effects). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study used task-based fMRI with whole-brain, group-level analyses and reports task-related activations in MNI space using BOLD contrast (satisfying I6, I7, I8, and I9). However, the experimental tasks are rhyme judgment (language) and mental rotation (spatial visualization), which are perceptual/processing tasks and do not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5 not met). Therefore the paper does not address problem-solving across domains as required and must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) were triggered.

The study uses a task-based BOLD fMRI Tower of London (ToL) planning paradigm, which is a problem-solving task (goal-directed planning). It reports whole-brain, group-level effects for the ToL (main effect of increasing task load) with whole-brain FWE-corrected results and reports stereotactic (MNI) coordinates for task-related activations (e.g., left medial dorsolateral PFC: x=-27 y=30 z=24 for interaction). The sample includes healthy adult participants (controls) and the reported task activations are derived from group-level second-level analyses that include healthy adults. Thus the study satisfies inclusion criteria I5 (problem-solving task), I6 (whole-brain group-level analysis including healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinate reporting), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (coordinates/results available within text/tables/analyses). Although the sample also includes MDD patients, the presence of healthy adults and whole-brain task effects makes this eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis focused on problem-solving in healthy adults.

This is an empirical, task-based BOLD fMRI study of arithmetic problem solving (a bona fide problem-solving task). It includes longitudinal and cross-sectional whole-brain analyses with group-level effects that include a healthy adult group (n=20) and reports whole-brain contrasts (addition vs control) using stereotactic MNI coordinates for activation peaks. The paper reports BOLD fMRI results and voxelwise analyses (whole-brain and searchlight/multivoxel), with coordinates provided in the main text and figures. It is not ROI-only, not a non-empirical paper, and includes within-group task effects for healthy adults. The supplied full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so appears complete for screening.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=42) using BOLD fMRI during mental arithmetic tasks (multiplication and subtraction), which qualify as problem-solving (goal-directed computation). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses (one-sample t-tests) with stereotactic coordinates in MNI space, and includes voxelwise results presented in tables/figures as well as ROI analyses. All required criteria are met: task-based fMRI of a problem-solving task (I5), whole-brain group analyses in healthy adults (I6), coordinates in MNI space (I7), BOLD fMRI analyses (I8), and reporting of voxelwise coordinate results in main text/figures (I9). Full text appears complete (background, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria apply.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation including a mental calculation task (silent subtraction), which meets the review definition of a problem-solving task (goal: compute result; requires figuring out procedure). It reports whole-brain random-effects group analyses on 81 healthy adult subjects, provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space, and uses BOLD fMRI (3T EPI) with voxelwise results presented in figures/tables. The full text includes background, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text is complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is excluded. Exclusion criteria met: E3 (reports only ROI results) — the authors conducted ROI-based analyses and explicitly state a whole-brain approach was not used; E5 (doesn't include any healthy-group task effect) — the analysis uses extant fMRI datasets drawn from participants with Williams syndrome only (no healthy adult group-level task effects are reported for the current analyses). Inclusion criteria met: I8 (reports BOLD analyses) — the study uses fMRI BOLD measures. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is not a problem-solving task; tasks are passive listening/viewing with low cognitive load), I6 (does not include whole-brain, group-level effects in healthy adults), I7 (no stereotactic coordinate results for whole-brain task effects in healthy adults), I9 (no voxelwise whole-brain results reported for healthy adults). Full text appears complete for screening. Therefore the paper does not meet the meta-analysis requirements.

This is a task-based fMRI study of propositional analogical reasoning (a fluid reasoning/problem-solving task) that includes healthy adult participants and reports group-level whole-brain analyses. The manuscript presents voxelwise whole-brain contrasts and multiple regression results with stereotactic coordinates (e.g., left RLPFC at −27, 50, 0; right RLPFC at 27, 45, 16), and uses BOLD fMRI. Results are reported across whole-brain maps and ROI follow-ups; they are not limited to ROI-only analyses. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, allowing assessment against inclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, task-based whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults using a syllogistic deductive-reasoning task. The reasoning task meets the review’s problem-solving definition (participants have the goal of deciding whether a conclusion follows and must determine how to reach that decision). The study reports group-level random-effects whole-brain analyses (SPM8), reports stereotactic MNI coordinates in the text and supplementary tables/figures, and uses BOLD fMRI analyses. Voxelwise results are reported in supplementary tables and main text figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not a non-empirical paper, includes healthy-group task effects). Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based whole-brain BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults (n≈15 in imaging analyses) using a reasoning task (syllogistic inference) where participants had the explicit goal to judge whether a conclusion follows from premises (i.e., goal-directed computation fitting the provided problem-solving definition). Group-level, whole-brain analyses are reported with stereotactic MNI coordinates for task-related activations and interaction contrasts. BOLD (fMRI) analyses are used and voxelwise results are reported in the main text and supplementary tables. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not limited to ROIs, participants are healthy adults, task effects within the healthy group are reported, and the paper is empirical with original data. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study uses the Tower of London (ToL) planning task, which qualifies as a problem-solving paradigm (I5), and it reports stereotactic coordinates (I7) from BOLD fMRI analyses (I8) with coordinates available in the text (I9). However, it does not present a whole-brain, group-level task activation map for healthy adults relevant to problem-solving. The reported imaging results focus on genotype-related correlations and diagnosis-by-genotype interactions (including ROI-based PFC findings) rather than reporting whole-brain task-related group effects in the healthy control group. The authors report that no other areas emerged as significant in whole-brain analyses for the ToL, and the principal ToL effects appear to be reported within an ROI framework. Therefore the study fails to meet inclusion criterion I6 and meets exclusion criterion E5 (doesn't include healthy-group task effects/only between-group/genotype contrasts relevant to this review). Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults that reports MNI coordinates and BOLD results (meets I6, I7, I8, I9). However, the experimental paradigm is multiple object tracking (MOT) investigating sensorimotor prediction/attention, not a problem-solving task as defined (a task with an explicit goal plus a need to figure out a way to reach it). Therefore I5 (study of a problem-solving task) is not satisfied. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Conclusion: EXCLUDE because it does not meet I5 (problem-solving task).

This is a task-based fMRI study of problem solving (compound remote associate problems) in healthy adults, using whole-brain, group-level random-effects analysis reporting BOLD results. The paper reports stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space (e.g., peak at 44, -9, -9) and describes whole-brain cluster-thresholding procedures. Thus it satisfies I5 (task-based problem solving), I6 (whole-brain group-level analysis in healthy adults), I7 (reports Talairach coordinates), I8 (BOLD/fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results available in text/figures). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not patient/group-comparison only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adult novice participants performing a multiple-choice electric-circuit task that requires judging correctness (a goal-directed problem-solving/decision task). The study reports whole-brain group-level SPM analyses on BOLD data, provides stereotactic MNI coordinates and tables/figures of task-related activations, and voxelwise results are reported. All inclusion criteria (I5–I9) are satisfied, and none of the exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This study is excluded because it does not meet key inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (it includes group-level fMRI analysis in healthy adults) and I8 (reports BOLD fMRI analysis). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (the task is a similarity-judgment/working-memory labeling task, not a problem-solving task as defined by a goal plus needing to figure out a way to reach it) and I7 (the full text does not report stereotactic coordinates in Talairach/MNI space for task-related activations in the provided content). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study is a whole-brain, task-based fMRI experiment in healthy adults with group-level random effects analyses and reports MNI coordinates and BOLD results. However, it does NOT investigate a problem-solving task as defined (a task that first has a goal and then requires figuring out a way to reach it). Instead, participants made communicative/strategic vs control judgments about social scenarios (moral/communication evaluation), which is not a goal-directed problem-solving paradigm. Therefore inclusion criterion I5 is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criteria not met: I5. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

Full text unavailable (only title/metadata provided). Cannot verify any inclusion criteria. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met / could not be confirmed: I5 (task-based fMRI/PET problem-solving task), I6 (whole-brain group-level analysis in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinate reporting in Talairach/MNI), I8 (BOLD or rCBF analysis reported), I9 (voxelwise results availability). No exclusion criteria met based on available information. Full text is incomplete, so study must be excluded until full text is obtained for assessment.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants performing single-digit multiplication problems (a problem-solving task). It reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses, including contrasts of interest (large vs. small problems) and inter-group comparisons. Results are reported as stereotactic coordinates in MNI space and derive from BOLD fMRI analyses; voxelwise cluster results are presented (tables/figures). The provided full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply.

Although this is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of an arithmetic problem-solving task in healthy adults with group-level whole-brain analyses and BOLD contrasts reported, the provided full text does not explicitly report stereotactic peak coordinates (Talairach or MNI) for task-related increases in the main text. While ROI center coordinates (from a meta-analysis) and references to Figures/Tables are present, explicit voxelwise peak coordinates for the reported activations are not shown in the provided material. Therefore the study fails to meet inclusion criterion I7 (reporting stereotactic coordinate results) and cannot be included. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I8, I9. Inclusion criterion not met: I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion) so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This study used an N-Back working memory task (a continuous performance/working memory paradigm), not a problem-solving task as defined by the review (goal-directed problem solving requiring figuring out a way to reach a goal). Although it is a task-based, whole-brain BOLD fMRI study with group analyses, the provided full text does not report stereotactic coordinates (Talairach/MNI) for task-related activations in the excerpt, and the task domain does not match the meta-analysis target (problem solving). Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria for the review.

This study does not meet I5 (problem-solving task). The experiments are categorical and coordinate spatial judgment tasks (perceptual/decision tasks) rather than problem-solving paradigms that require setting a goal and devising a means/strategy to reach it. It does meet I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI analyses reported), I7 (results/methods report MNI stereotactic coordinates), I8 (task-based BOLD fMRI reported), and I9 (voxelwise/ROI and whole-brain results are described and available). No exclusion criteria are triggered (E3, E4, E5, E6 not applicable). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore excluded because it fails the essential inclusion criterion I5.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using BOLD contrast in healthy adult participants (20 licensed taxi drivers). The task is goal-directed navigation delivering customers to destinations, requiring subjects to plan routes and solve problems in real-time, meeting the definition of a problem-solving task (goal plus need to figure out a way to reach it). The analysis is whole-brain (SPM2 preprocessing and random-effects second-level t-tests), reporting stereotactic coordinates in MNI space and voxelwise results (tables/figures) for task-related increases. Thus it satisfies I5–I9 and does not violate any exclusion criteria. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

Excluded (E3): The study reports PET results using predefined ROI analyses (regional binding potentials) rather than a whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analysis. Inclusion met: I5 — it is a task-based PET study using an attentive calculation task (problem-focused calculation) in healthy adults. Inclusion NOT met: I6 — no whole-brain voxelwise/group-level whole-brain analysis is reported; I7 — no stereotactic (Talairach/MNI) coordinate results are provided; I8 — the outcomes are PET receptor binding potentials (BP) for H1 receptors, not task-related BOLD or rCBF measures. Full text appears complete. Based on these, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

Although this is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that reports whole-brain, group-level BOLD results with stereotactic (MNI) coordinates, it does not meet the review’s operational definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The experiment investigates category-based induction and the inclusion fallacy — a comparative semantic/reasoning judgment about which of two inductive arguments is stronger — rather than a goal-directed problem-solving paradigm that requires establishing a goal and figuring out means to achieve it (e.g., planning, multi-step solution search). Therefore I5 is not satisfied. All other inclusion criteria (I6, I7, I8, I9) are met. No exclusion criteria are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (n=11, mean age 26.9) using auditory multidigit addition (a goal-directed problem-solving task) with blocked task blocks. The study reports whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects group analyses, uses BOLD fMRI, and provides stereotactic coordinates normalized to MNI space (with supplementary tables/figures reporting task-related activations). All inclusion criteria are satisfied (I5–I9). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not clinical-group-only, includes within-healthy-group task effects). The provided full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Based on these factors, the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults performing a simple mental calculation (X×Y+Z), so it meets I5 (task with a goal needing a method), I6 (whole-brain group-level analysis in healthy adults), and I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis). However, the full text does not report stereotactic coordinates (Talairach or MNI) for task-related increases in the manuscript or tables; activations are shown as figures/voxel maps but no coordinates are provided, so it fails I7 and I9. Because reporting of standardized coordinates is required for inclusion in this coordinate-based meta-analysis, the study must be excluded. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults that reports BOLD results as stereotactic coordinates (MNI) for group-level effects. However, the experimental task investigates humor comprehension/incongruity resolution (reading/verbal jokes) rather than a problem-solving task as defined by the review (having a goal and needing to figure out a way to reach it). Therefore it does not meet inclusion criterion I5 and must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This study is excluded because it does not investigate a problem-solving task (I5 not met). It is a methods/rtfMRI validation study using a finger-tapping motor task. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI analysis in healthy adults), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), I9 (voxelwise results/activation maps indicated in text/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (not a problem-solving task), I7 (the full text does not clearly present stereotactic coordinate tables of task-related increases in Talairach/MNI space). Exclusion criteria met: none []. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is excluded because participants are adolescents (mean ages 16.8 and 16.9), not healthy adults as required by inclusion criterion I6. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI mental-rotation task meeting the review’s problem-solving definition), I7 (task-related stereotactic coordinates reported in MNI space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis reported), I9 (voxelwise whole-brain results reported in figures/tables). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (requires healthy adult participants; sample is adolescent). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered by the report. Full text appears complete for screening (introduction, methods, results, discussion provided).

This is a behavioral study of arithmetic (reaction times and strategy ratings) in healthy adults; it does not include any task-based fMRI or PET data, whole-brain group-level analyses, stereotactic coordinates, or BOLD/rCBF results. Full text is complete. Exclusion rationale: No imaging modalities or voxelwise results reported. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (not a task-based fMRI or PET study), I6 (no whole-brain group-level analysis), I7 (no stereotactic coordinate results in Talairach/MNI), I8 (no BOLD or rCBF analysis), I9 (not applicable—no voxelwise results to report). Exclusion criteria met: none of the listed exclusion IDs (E3–E6) directly apply; exclusion is based on failure to meet required inclusion criteria. Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis focused on whole-brain task-based fMRI/PET problem-solving studies.

(a) Exclusion IDs met: none. This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants investigating analogical reasoning. The task requires establishing a goal and deriving the correct response by integrating spatial relations and inhibiting superficial responses, which fits the review's definition of problem solving/critical thinking. The study reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses with multiple-comparison correction, provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (e.g., R IFG x=52,y=40,z=10), and analyzes BOLD signal. Voxelwise and ROI results are presented in the main text. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9, and no exclusion criteria are met.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of four-term analogical reasoning in healthy adult participants, which qualifies as problem solving (inferring a target D based on an A:B relation and mapping/inference processes). It reports whole-brain group-level analyses normalized to MNI space, presents task-related BOLD activation, and provides stereotactic coordinates (MNI) for activation peaks. Though ROI analyses are used, whole-brain results and coordinates are reported, so it does not meet the ROI-only exclusion. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9) and no exclusion criteria apply.

Although this is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults reporting BOLD results in Talairach space (and voxelwise results), the experimental task is empathic/emotional state reasoning (inferring causes of facial expressions from four candidate situations). This does not meet the meta-analysis definition of a problem-solving task (I5) which requires goal-directed problem solving involving evaluation, planning/sequencing actions, and executing operations under a rule set to arrive at a (sometimes novel) solution. The present task is an emotion inference/forced-choice matching task rather than planning, sequencing, or rule-based problem solving across domains. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5. No exclusion criteria (E3-E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

The study is an event-related fMRI investigation of angle discrimination (visuospatial perceptual task) in healthy adults. It does include whole-brain group-level analyses and reports BOLD results (satisfying I6 and I8). However, it does not examine a problem-solving task as defined by the review (no evidence of goal-directed problem solving, planning, sequencing of actions, or application of rule-based operations to derive novel solutions) so it fails I5. In the provided full text there are no stereotactic coordinate tables or explicit Talairach/MNI coordinates shown, so I7 is not clearly satisfied from the excerpt. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI empirical study of abstract reasoning (a form of problem solving) that meets the review definitions: (1) the abstract reasoning task requires goal-directed solution of novel sequences and higher-order planning/relational operations, satisfying I5; (2) it reports whole-brain, group-level effects including a one-sample (controls) and between-group analyses (I6); (3) stereotactic coordinates are provided in MNI space for activations (I7); (4) results are from BOLD fMRI (I8); (5) voxelwise results/coordinates are reported in tables and figures (I9). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is present. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Therefore include.

The study is a task-based fMRI experiment in healthy adult participants performing goal-directed, rule-based mental-operation tasks (numeral addition, spatial marker movement, verbal sequencing). These tasks meet the review’s problem-solving definition (I5). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses in healthy adults (I6), provides stereotactic coordinates (MNI) for task-related activations (I7), uses BOLD fMRI (I8), and reports voxelwise results/coordinates in the text (I9). No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are not ROI-only, not limited to disease/age/gender comparisons, include within-group task effects for healthy participants, and are empirical. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so content is complete.

This is a task-based, event-related fMRI study of verbal analogical reasoning in healthy adults that meets the review objective. It uses a problem-solving/analogy task requiring goal-directed retrieval, integration, and evaluation (qualifies as problem solving). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses, provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (tables/figures), and analyzes BOLD signal (event-related fMRI). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the record is complete for screening.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of relational reasoning (Raven’s Progressive Matrices adaptation), which qualifies as a problem-solving task (goal-directed identification and execution of rules to infer a missing matrix element). The study includes healthy adult participants (18-25 years) and reports whole-brain analyses (FIR, whole-brain two-sample t-tests, group-level contrasts) and adult group activation patterns. Data were normalized to MNI space and the manuscript references coordinate-containing results (Supplementary Table, figures), satisfying stereotactic reporting. BOLD fMRI analyses are explicitly reported. Voxelwise/whole-brain results are presented in figures/tables/supplementary materials. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; empirical with healthy adult task effects). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; core content appears complete.

This is a task-based, whole-brain BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults that examines rule-based manipulation within working memory. The manipulation trials require subjects to apply prelearned reordering rules to achieve a goal, which fits the review's problem-solving definition (goal-directed, planning/sequencing/rule-based operations to arrive at a correct solution). The study reports group-level, random-effects whole-brain analyses in MNI stereotaxic space, provides voxelwise results and figures/tables, and uses BOLD fMRI contrasts. All required inclusion criteria are satisfied (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion and appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of problem solving (arithmetic Pyramid and Formula problems) in healthy adult participants (n=20). It includes whole-brain analyses (classification using whole-brain mega-voxels and exploratory whole-brain contrasts), reports group-level effects, and provides stereotactic coordinates (Talairach coordinates cited for HIPS and angular gyrus). The study uses BOLD fMRI and reports voxelwise results (with cluster thresholds and coordinates referenced). All specified inclusion criteria are met (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This PET study in healthy adult participants reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM99) of task-related rCBF changes, including stereotactic coordinates in standardized space. The complex mental calculation task (2x2-digit multiplications) clearly meets the review’s definition of problem solving (goal-directed arithmetic operations requiring planning/sequencing and rule-based execution). Whole-brain PET rCBF analyses and conjunction/contrast results are reported with coordinates; results are not ROI-only. Full methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9 are met, and no exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study includes an explicit deductive reasoning (logic) localizer task that meets the review's definition of problem-solving (goal-directed deductive inference using rule-based logical operations). It reports group-level whole-brain fMRI analyses in healthy adult participants, with task-related activations reported as stereotactic Talairach coordinates and BOLD-based measures. The full text contains methods, results (including whole-brain contrasts and coordinate tables), and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5 (task-based problem-solving/logical task), I6 (whole-brain group-level effects in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported in Talairach space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results presented in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants (university students) that uses a mental-arithmetic verification task ((a×b)−c=d) that fits the review’s operational definition of problem solving (goal-directed algebraic operations requiring planning/sequencing and rule-based execution). The study reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM analyses on transformed Talairach-space data, uses BOLD fMRI, and provides voxelwise/ROI results in tables/figures (and supplementary materials), satisfying coordinate reporting. Participants are healthy adults and task effects (math>word and cue/task contrasts) are explicitly analyzed. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not non-empirical, includes within-group task effects in healthy subjects). Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete for screening purposes.
